question.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ -11\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ -11\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1} \\ 7{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ -11\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=4 \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=-11\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $(-2)$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1} & =-9\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5(3)+2{x}_{2} & =4\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-\frac{11}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=-\frac{11}{2}$ into the third equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & =-11 \\ -(3)+3(-\frac{11}{2}) & =-11 \\ -\frac{33}{2} & =-8,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement. 

So, the system has no solution.
